title: Annotatio VI §.III (1): Augustine — Peter panem Dominum; Judas panem Domini / penalty
pass_a_gloss: For (1) concerning the first of all who communicate unworthily, Judas the betrayer, Augustine’s judgment is commonly known, pronounced in comparing him with communicating Peter — that Peter and Judas received from one bread, a part of the same bread, from the same Lord’s hand (Tract. in Joh. 56; and Tom. post. collat. against the Donatists); yet meanwhile that one, Peter, received the bread the Lord, but this one, Judas, only the bread of the Lord against the Lord — Peter, life (because Christ’s flesh which vivifies), but Judas, penalty (because impious, the blessed bread which draws judgment). Tract. 59.
pass_b_english: (1) On Judas, first unworthy communicant: Augustine compares him with Peter — same bread, same Lord’s hand (Tract. Joh. 56; against the Donatists).
Yet Peter received the bread the Lord (life — vivifying flesh); Judas only the bread of the Lord against the Lord (penalty — blessed bread that draws judgment). Tract. 59.
source_text: Nam (1) de indignè Communicante omnium primo, Juda proditore, in vulgus notum est, Augustini judicium, in comparatione hujus cum communicante Petro, latum ac pronunciatum, quô Petrum & Judam, de uno quidem pane, ejusdémque panis partem, de eadem Dominica manu, accepisse, ait, Tractat. in Joh. 56. & Tom. post. collat. contr. Donatist.; interim tamen illum, seu Petrum, panem Dominum, hunc verò, seu Judam, panem duntaxat Domini, contra Dominum — Petrum, vitam (quia carnem Christi, quæ vivificat), Judam verò pœnam (quia impius, panem benedictum, qui judicium attrahit) accepisse. Tract. 59.
